newsitem.title: USA: Outright losses dampen cash crude dealings in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Outright losses dampen cash crude dealings in U.S..

text.p: Paper market losses deflated outright U.S. cash crude prices Monday morning in a sluggishly traded session to start the week.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing ranged 15-20 cents weaker at $19.65-75 a barrel, and held a 5-8 cents discount to second month October values.

Traders said the cash side of the market began slowly, with only a few confirmed grade parcels switching hands. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold at 20 cent over the September benchmark, and a late August/September roll moved at -18 cents, traders said.
Other prices for the grades held steady, with West Texas Sour/Midland at a $1.65-58 discount and September Postings Plus at $1.95-$2.00.
Outright prices saw profit-taking eat away at the bottom line. Traders said developments on the Iraqi oil sales front softened the market too.

Baghdad was expected to submit annexes to the main aid distribution plan document later Monday. Once the annexes are reviewed by the U.N., the process for approving the aid plan and resuming oil exports can be accelerated under the stalled "oil-for-food" accord.
Western diplomats and U.N. officials said aid plan approval was still eyed before the end of the week.
